conviction_note: Fuel is the whole story: AERO's July guide assumed $3.2/gal for Q3 and $3.0 for Q4, while peers guiding the same week assumed $3.50-3.69, Delta realised $3.80 GAAP in Q3, and the October curve is around $4.25-4.95. So a Q3 margin shortfall and a sharp Q4/FY guide reset are near-certain. The market can see all of that (the CEO flagged fuel in the August and September traffic releases, and the stock is 30% off its high and flat for 20 days), and Delta's own fuel-driven guide cut cost it only about 3%. Strong Latin/transborder pricing (Delta Latin unit revenue +22%) offsets part of it on revenue. Net: a small negative lean (p_up 45) on a guidance-reset scale of about 6%. impact_sum (-1.3) and the scaled number (-0.65) agree in sign; the scaled number is smaller because sign confidence is low.
bar: Revenue: company guide 3Q26 $1.59-1.62bn (midpoint $1.605bn), op margin 14-17%, adj EBITDAR margin 26.5-29.5%, assumptions fuel $3.2/gal all-in and MXN 17.5 (6-K Ex.99.1, 2026-07-13, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001561861/000119312526302103/d112634dex991.htm). The EPS consensus is unsourced and disputed: TipRanks 0.61 (zero analysts), Benzinga 0.43, Tickflow 0.24 on $1.55bn revenue (https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mx:aero/earnings, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AERO/earnings-forecasts, https://tickflow.io/stock/AERO/forecast). Findings are sized against the company guide, not EPS, and kept small because the street bar after fuel is unknown. print_vs_bar_pct is revenue against the guide midpoint.
positioning_check: Short interest about 0.7% of float per Benzinga (undated, retrieved 2026-10-19, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AERO/sentiment); the sweep notes other vendors disagree wildly, and days to cover were not found. Not a crowded short. Options: skew_25d is null, total OI only 200, put/call OI 0.05, ATM spread 33% of mid. The 11.39% event-implied move rests on a nearly untraded chain and is not a reliable anchor. Tape: run-up 5d +0.31%, 20d +1.07%, -29.6% from the 52-week high. Confirmed earnings reactions were Q2 (released 2026-07-13 amc) +2.29% and Q1 (released 2026-04-21) about -4.9%; the rest of the baseline history is monthly traffic 6-Ks.

findings.finding: AERO's 3Q26 guide (op margin 14-17%, adj EBITDAR 26.5-29.5%) was built on $3.2/gal all-in fuel. Peers guiding the same week used higher numbers: United $3.69 all-in (July 14 curve), Volaris $3.50 Gulf Coast. Delta then realised $3.80 GAAP / $3.61 adjusted in Q3 and absorbed $500m+ more fuel than its July forecast. AERO paid $4.20 in Q2, close to United's $4.19, so its Q3 fuel was likely around $3.8-4.0, about $0.6-0.8/gal (~$70-95m, ~5pp of margin on ~$1.6bn revenue) above its own assumption before recapture. Reported operating margin will likely land below the 14-17% guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: op margin 4.6% landed at the low end of the 4-7% guide on $4.20 fuel and EPS -$0.40 missed -$0.37; the stock rose +2.29% the next session (baseline 2026-07-13 amc). Q1: margin at the low end of guide, about -4.9%. The holders have looked through fuel-driven margin misses before.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The CEO wrote 'higher jet fuel prices continue to create a more challenging cost environment than anticipated' in the September traffic release, and Delta's fuel miss was public on 10-09. If no one had priced it, the EPS estimates would cluster near last year's $1.2; they range $0.24-0.61. What may be unpriced is how far below peers AERO's $3.2 assumption sat: a model that haircut the guide by a peer-sized fuel gap would still be too high.
findings.independence: Delta Q3 8-K, 2026-10-09 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000027904/000002790426000035/deltaairlinesannouncessept.htm); United Q2 8-K Q3 fuel assumption (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000100517/000010051726000135/ual_erx06302026xex992.htm); Volaris Q2 guide (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/controladora-vuela-compania-de-aviacion-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-22/); AERO September traffic CEO quote (https://finviz.com/news/399318/aeromexico-september-2026-traffic-results). Shares the July 6-K with the Q4 guide finding, but this one is the Q3 line and that one is the Q4/FY line.

findings.finding: AERO's 4Q26 guide (op margin 15.5-18.5%, EBITDAR 28-31%) and FY26 guide (op margin 11-13%, EBITDAR 24-26%) assume $3.0/gal. The forward curve has moved far above that: Delta's 4Q guide uses the 2026-10-02 curve, about $4.25 all-in after a ~$0.40 refinery benefit; NY jet hit $4.95 on 2026-10-10 (Bloomberg via aggregator); Gulf Coast peaked at $4.705 on Sept 15. With ~125m Q4 gallons, a $1.2-1.5/gal gap is ~$150-190m, about 9-11pp of Q4 margin before recapture. The peso also weakened to 17.97 by 30 September against a 17.6 Q4 assumption. A large Q4/FY guide cut is near-certain on the 20 October call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No confirmed AERO reaction to a guide cut since the November 2025 IPO. Q1 2026, when FY guidance was withdrawn and Q2 was guided to 4-7%, drew about -4.9%. Closest peer analog: Delta cut FY EPS from $6.50-7.50 to $5.10-5.60 on fuel on 2026-10-09 and fell about 3%, inside its ~4% implied move (https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx).
findings.why_not_priced: The direction is priced: the stock is 30% off its high and the fuel curve is public. The size may not be. AERO's $3.0 Q4 assumption sits further below the curve than US peers' assumptions did, AERO has no refinery offset, and it already ran a 4.6% op margin in a $4.20 quarter. If the cut were fully priced, AERO would have fallen when Delta cut on 10-09 and jet set new highs on 10-10; instead it is flat over 20 days.
findings.independence: Jet price path: GlobalAir/Flycraft Gulf Coast spot (https://www.flycraft.com/jet-fuel-price); Bloomberg via aggregator on Oct 10 highs (https://stockhub.kr/en/news/news_f45cea4bff87); peso at 17.97 on 2026-09-30 (https://www.eldolar.info/es-MX/mexico/dia/20260930). Guide assumptions come from the same AERO 6-K as the Q3 finding.

findings.finding: Delta's 3Q26 Latin America unit revenue rose +22% y/y, with yield +20% on -6% capacity, the strongest of its regions. Its Latin entity includes the Mexico transborder JV with AERO, which a court kept intact on 2026-08-20. That points to strong transborder pricing. AERO said it recaptured 76% of incremental Q2 fuel through pricing and grew TRASM +10.5% in Q2. So Q3 revenue is likely at or above the $1.62bn top of guide, at roughly flat-to-slightly-above-guide capacity.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: record revenue of $1,479m (+12.6%) inside its guide, +2.29% next session alongside a margin at the low end. No confirmed instance of a revenue beat above guide since the IPO.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a counterparty's regional table, published after AERO last spoke (its September traffic release of 10-06 carries no revenue). Tickflow's $1.55bn revenue estimate sits below AERO's own guide floor, so at least one estimate set has not absorbed the yield strength. If it were priced, the estimates would sit at or above the $1.62bn top of guide.
findings.independence: AERO's Q2 6-K: TRASM +10.5%, yield +11.4% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001561861/000119312526302103/d112634dex991.htm). AERO's September traffic: international RPMs +6.6%, load factor 87.6% (https://finviz.com/news/399318/aeromexico-september-2026-traffic-results). Delta's Latin entity is broader than Mexico, so this is a proxy.

findings.finding: AERO's own monthly traffic puts Q3 capacity at roughly +1.3% y/y (July ASMs -1.5%, August +2.3%, September +3.4%), at the top of the +0.5-1.5% guide. Load factor was 88.0% / 89.7% / 87.1% (Aug and Sep up y/y, July down 0.4pp). Domestic passengers fell 3.9% while international RPMs rose. Volume is in line with guide and the mix is shifting toward higher-yield international.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Monthly traffic 6-Ks drew -4.7% to +4.8% moves in the baseline, but those are traffic days, not prints. On the print days volume was in line and not the driver.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. These are public monthly releases inside the company's guided capacity range. What remains is the mix effect on unit revenue.
findings.independence: July traffic (https://www.financialcontent.com/article/gnwcq-2026-8-3-aeromxico-july-2026-traffic-results); August traffic (https://finviz.com/news/388703/aeromexico-august-2026-traffic-results). Same company source family.

findings.finding: The peso traded stronger than the 17.5 Q3 assumption for most of the quarter (about 16.88-16.93 in early-to-mid September) before weakening to 17.97 on 30 September. That is a modest Q3 tailwind to USD-reported peso revenue and a modest headwind to the Q4 assumption of 17.6.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No instance of FX being the line on an AERO print.
findings.why_not_priced: Public spot rates. It is small, and the sign on AERO's net USD exposure is not disclosed in what I read, so it is filed small.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-20 the Eleventh Circuit vacated DOT's September 2025 order ending antitrust immunity for the Delta-Aeromexico JV, which keeps transborder revenue sharing intact. The call can cite JV continuity as support for the forward guide. It is priced: the stock rose +3.31% on 2026-08-21 in the baseline, and whether DOT will seek rehearing is not established.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: +3.31% on 2026-08-21 (baseline row, bmo), the session after the ruling.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced already. Only the call's commentary on any DOT rehearing or petition could add news.

A peer analog (Delta -3% on a fuel-driven cut) says that kind of guide reset draws a modest reaction. That keeps p_up only a little below 50, and there is no skew to argue with.
